title.suggested: Tom Allen and Jack Stewart Fight to a Draw in London

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported from London that Tom Allen and Jack Stewart of Scotland, fighting for the championship of the world, scarcely touched each other; the referee declared a draw after 24 rounds.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Wednesday Morning, April 23, 1879, page 3. Dispatch dated London, April 22.

facts.fact: Allen fought Jack Stewart of Scotland for the championship of the world (reported from London); they scarcely touched each other except in the seventh round, where Allen had a slight advantage, and after 24 rounds the referee declared the fight a draw and bets off
The Allen-Stewart fight was for £400 (figure partly legible; OCR reads £100)

notes: Current title mistranslates the headline 'Tom Allen Indulges in a "Barney"' (a barney = a sham or fixed fight), not a hairnet. The word after 'proved to be a complete f...' is cut off. Members of the aristocracy were reported among a large crowd.
